p:cNvPr.descr: The reactions between FAD and FMNH2, and the structures of the molecules involved. On the left is an FAD molecule, bracketed and labeled on the left, with the FMN portion bracketed and labeled as well. They are labeled at the bottom “flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) and flavin mononucleotide (FMN).” The whole molecule, from the bottom up, consists of a pentose ring bonded to adenine at the upper right. The CH2 on the left side of the pentose ring bonds up a phosphate group, beginning with O, which bonds up to P, which bonds left to O-, double bonds right to O, and bonds up to O. A pink dashed line bisects the top O horizontally; above this is a second identical phosphate group. This dashed line also marks the beginning of the part of the molecule that is FMN, labeled and bracketed on the left. The top O in the second phosphate group bonds up to CH2, which bonds up to CH2O, which bonds up to CH2O, which bonds up to CH2O, which bonds up to CH2. CH2 then bonds up to a series of three 6-sided ring structures. This is bracketed and labeled “isoalloxazine ring” at the top. The CH2 bonds up to N, which bonds up and right to C, which bonds up to C, which double bonds up and left to N, which bonds down and left to C. C double bonds down to C, which bonds down and right to the initial N. To the left is another ring structure, this time a 6-sided ring with 2 double bonds on the left side, the carbons of which are bonded up and left to CH3 and down and left to CH3. The ring on the ring begins on the bottom with N, which double bonds up and left to C, which bonds up to C, which bonds up and right to C. C double bonds up to O, then down and right to NH. NH bonds down to C, which double bonds down and right to O, then down and left to N. To the right is an equilibrium arrow with a convergent arrow on the top, labeled H+ + e-, indicating their addition. To the right of this arrow is an FADH molecule. The FADH has a small dot to the right of its name, indicating that it is a stable free radical. It is labeled FADH (FMNH) (semiquinone) at the bottom. Its structure is similar to the isoalloxazine ring described previously, the key difference being that the topmost N in the central ring is now bonded up to a blue H, and has a blue + sign to its upper right. There is a small blue dot just below the N, indicating that it has accepted only a single proton and is therefore a free radical. The bottom N of the central ring is now bonded down to an R group as well. To the right is an equilibrium arrow like the one described before, with a convergent arrow on top showing addition of H+ and e- (shown in blue). The structure to the right of this is the FADH2 (FMNH2) molecule, fully reduced, and labeled below. Here, the top N of the central ring is no longer radicalized; instead, it is bonded up to a blue H. The bottom N on the rightmost ring has also bonded down to a blue H.
